[crates/op-cache/DESIGN.md#A8AD]
1:# Btrfs cache, NUMA and timing
2:
3:The owner reaffirmed this architecture on 2026-09-23. It follows the original
4:`operation-dbus-proto` design in `branding/product-baseline.md` §12 and
5:`crates/op-snowball/{DESIGN,REQUIREMENTS}.md`, especially requirement R5.
6:The later global five-subvolume cap and directory-conversion rule are withdrawn.
7:
8:## Storage ownership
9:
10:The cache has a Btrfs root and five category subvolumes:
11:
12:```text
13:cache/                         Btrfs subvolume
14:  embeddings/                  Btrfs subvolume
15:  blocks/                      Btrfs subvolume
16:  queries/                     Btrfs subvolume
17:  diffs/                       Btrfs subvolume
18:  kv/                          Btrfs subvolume
19:```
20:
21:Reopening the cache preserves those subvolumes. An existing ordinary directory
22:on Btrfs is not silently converted, deleted or accepted as the intended
23:subvolume. The optional ordinary-filesystem cache path does not provide Btrfs
24:snapshot or transport semantics.
25:
26:Snowball separately owns the authoritative append-only timing stream and its
27:vector/state projections. Its timing, vector and state paths are Btrfs
28:subvolumes. Cache contents are rebuildable; they do not replace the timing
29:record, canonical event chain, identity credential or grants.
30:
31:## Snapshot and transfer contract
32:
33:A Btrfs snapshot of the cache root does not include its nested subvolume data.
34:Each cache snapshot set therefore contains six read-only snapshots: `root` and
35:one for every category. A completion marker is published only after every
36:member is verified. Send/receive transfers each member explicitly. A partial
37:set is not advertised as complete. Historical parent-only snapshots remain
38:preserved and are excluded from automatic rotation.
39:
40:Retention counts complete cache sets. Its default is 24, configurable with
41:`OPDBUS_MAX_CACHE_SNAPSHOTS`; zero is invalid. It is not a global subvolume cap.
42:Cache members are snapshotted sequentially, so complete coverage does not mean
43:one atomic instant across concurrent cache writers. Snowball's authoritative
44:timing/vector/state set uses its shared writer lock for consistent construction.
45:
46:## NUMA placement
47:
48:`OptimizedSnowball` detects topology and requests CPU affinity and preferred
49:memory placement on a dedicated writer thread. Timing, vectors and mirrored
50:cache blocks use that writer; Tokio worker threads are not pinned by this path.
51:CPU affinity, memory-policy acceptance and actual memory locality are distinct.
52:Neither a successful constructor nor a Btrfs subvolume proves physical NUMA
53:placement. Verify the live writer's CPU mask and report memory-policy failures
54:separately. Placement failures must not erase or weaken durable timing records.
55:
56:## Verification
57:
58:Native fixture tests must check reopen, child data in snapshots, read-only
59:members, actual send/receive, preservation of historical sets and category roots,
60:and the real writer's affinity after a write. Send/receive tests need the
61:necessary Btrfs privileges and an isolated fixture. Passing parser or ordinary
62:filesystem tests alone does not establish that this path works on the host.
